# std.timetree

Offline segment tree over time (divide-and-conquer on life intervals).  Turn any rollback-capable data structure (e.g. `Dsu` with `.mark()` / `.undo_to(snap)`) into a dynamic structure with insertions and deletions over `[0, q)` in O(q log q) apply/undo steps.

Import: `use std.timetree.{...}`.

## `enum TimeStep`

One step in a `TimeTree` DFS traversal: - `Apply(id)`: apply event `tt.event(id)` on entry to a segment-tree node.

## `struct TimeTree<E>`

Offline segment tree over time `[0, q)` holding events of type `E` active on half-open intervals `[lo, hi)`.

Fields: `q: Int`, `size: Int`, `ev_val: List<E>`.

- `fn new(q: Int) -> TimeTree<E>` — O(q) time and memory; An empty timeline of `q` time slots `0..q`, with no events scheduled yet.; traps: when `q < 0`
- `fn add_interval(mut self, lo: Int, hi: Int, ev: E)` — O(log q); Schedule `ev` to be active at every time slot in `lo..hi` (half-open).; traps: when `lo < 0` or `hi > q` on a non-empty interval
- `fn event(self, id: Int) -> E` — O(1); The event carried by `TimeStep.Apply(id)`.; traps: when `id` is not an id that some `Apply` step carries
- `fn steps(self) -> List<TimeStep>` — O(q + m log q) time and memory for `m` scheduled intervals; The whole depth-first walk over `0..q` as a list.
- `fn run<M, R>(self, mark: () -> M, apply: E -> (), answer: Int -> R, undo: M -> ()) -> List<R>` — O(q + m log q) callback calls for `m` scheduled intervals, O(log q) extra stack; Walk the same order as `steps` with callbacks instead of a list.; traps: never (callbacks may trap)
- `fn add_range(mut self, r: Range<Int>, ev: E)` — O(log q); Schedule `ev` to be active at every time slot in `r`; `add_interval` with the range form.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `0..q`
- `fn walk(self) -> yields TimeStep` — O(1) amortized per step, O(log q) extra stack; The steps of `steps`, yielded one at a time without building the list.

## Functions

- `fn cdq<E>(events: List<E>, on_cross: (List<E>, List<E>) -> ())` — O(n log n) plus the callbacks; each level copies the halves, O(n) extra memory; CDQ divide and conquer over `events` in their given order.; traps: never (the callback may trap)
- `fn offline_over<E, M, R>(q: Int, items: List<E>, by: E -> (Int, Int), mark: () -> M, apply: E -> (), answer: Int -> R, undo: M -> ()) -> List<R>` — O(q + m log q) callback calls for `m` items; Offline divide and conquer over time `0..q`: each item is active on the half-open slots `by(item) = (lo, hi)`.; traps: when an item's non-empty interval reaches outside `0..q`

## Example

```cp
use std.timetree.{TimeTree}
var tt = TimeTree<Int>(4)
tt.add_range(0..4, 1)
print(yes(tt.steps().len > 0))
// output: YES
```
